title: CodeGrep: An RL-Trained Retrieval Agent for LLM Coding Agents
event_hint: A 14B RL-trained agent-style code retriever (CodeGrep) that emits multi-turn parallel grep/glob/read calls and feeds candidate files to a frozen OpenHands agent, cutting rounds and tokens on SWE-Bench Verified while slightly lifting resolve rate.
problem: LLM coding agents (Claude Code, OpenHands) spend most of their token budget finding the file to patch rather than patching it. On SWE-Bench Verified a 30B OpenHands agent averages 23 rounds and 631K tokens per resolved issue, dominated by grep/glob/view_file calls in ambiguous exploration loops, often 20+ rounds in a wrong direction before giving up. No open, systematically-studied agent-style code retriever exists at scale to shorten this phase.
mechanism: CodeGrep is a 14B-parameter retriever built on Qwen3-14B-Instruct, trained end-to-end with GRPO in a custom Git-worktree RL environment. It exposes three read-only primitives (grep regex search, glob path matching, read file contents), emitting up to 8 concurrent tool calls per turn and up to 4 turns (3 exploration + 1 answer). Candidate files are injected into the prompt of a frozen, untouched OpenHands downstream agent, so any downstream effect is unambiguously attributable to the retriever. Supervision is mined via CATM from 67K open-source OpenHands trajectories (one-to-many attribution). A reward-design study (v1->v2->v3) shows that applying the efficiency signal at the advantage layer rather than the reward layer holds KL drift to roughly one-third, and that dropping an auxiliary line-range component improves both stability and downstream efficiency.

evidence.claim: On all 500 SWE-Bench Verified instances, CodeGrep v3 lifts resolve rate by +1.2pp (25.8%->27.0%) while cutting resolved rounds 23.0->19.6 (-15%) and resolved tokens 631K->514K (-19%) versus the no-retrieval OpenHands baseline. Section 5.3 caveat: these headline numbers are pooled over each configuration's OWN resolved set (baseline 129, v3 135) and therefore mix a genuine efficiency effect with a selection effect; on the 96 paired instances both configurations resolve, rounds fall 20.1->18.3 (-9%) and tokens 525K->448K (-15%), preserving 60-80% of the pooled effect and confirming the improvement as per-issue acceleration rather than a selection artifact.
evidence.value: 27.0% resolve; pooled -15% rounds/-19% tokens; paired -9% rounds/-15% tokens on 96 co-resolved
evidence.baseline: No-retrieval OpenHands + Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507: 25.8% resolve, 23.0 rounds, 631K tokens per resolved instance
evidence.condition: 500 SWE-Bench Verified instances; pooled accounting over each config's own resolved set; paired-instance accounting restricted to 96 co-resolved instances; frozen downstream agent
evidence.source_locator: Section 4.3 / Table 3 (PDF Page 6); Section 5.3 'Pooled vs. paired-instance efficiency' (PDF Page 8)

evidence.claim: Downstream utility follows a precision threshold across three retrievers: BM25 (file-precision 0.375) degrades the agent (resolve -0.6pp, resolved tokens +21%, 631K->763K); Jina (0.445) is neutral (resolve identical to baseline 25.8%, tokens -7%); only CodeGrep (0.677) crosses the threshold at which retrieval buys efficiency.
evidence.value: BM25 0.375 hurts; Jina 0.445 neutral; CodeGrep 0.677 helps
evidence.condition: Injected into the same frozen OpenHands + Qwen3-30B-A3B agent
evidence.source_locator: Section 5.1 and Section 4.3, PDF Page 6; precision figures from Table 2

evidence.claim: Intrinsic retrieval quality (Table 2): CodeGrep v3 reaches file-precision 0.677, recall 0.435, F-beta mean 0.576, 43.0% of cases at F-beta>=0.8, in 2.3 agentic turns, versus BM25 (precision 0.375, recall 0.386, 7.0% F-beta>=0.8) and Jina-1.5B (precision 0.445, recall 0.468, 7.0%).
evidence.value: CodeGrep v3 precision 0.677 / recall 0.435 / 43.0% F-beta>=0.8 / 2.3 turns
evidence.condition: Internal evaluation set; turns column applies only to the agentic retriever

evidence.claim: Reward-design study: reward-layer multiplicative scaling of a tool-call penalty (v1) drives KL-to-reference to ~0.31 by step 900, while advantage-layer scaling (v2/v3) holds KL at 0.09/0.15 (~one-third); v3 also converges higher on reward (0.60-0.65 vs 0.45-0.48 for v1/v2) and stabilizes tool-use turns at ~2.1 vs rebound to ~2.6 for v1/v2. Removing the auxiliary line-range term (F_beta^lr) eliminates a signal with no downstream consumer (the editor takes no line ranges) and is systematically zero on CATM-only entries.
evidence.source_locator: Section 3.5 and Figure 2, PDF Pages 2 and 5; Table 1, PDF Page 5; v3 discussion Section 5.2, PDF Page 8

evidence.claim: Engineering scale: supervision mined from 67,074 raw OpenHands trajectories, filtered by a GLM-5.1-FP8 judge (16-way parallel, thresholds reasoning_tokens>=30 and w>=0.15) to 31,977 effective training samples (47.7% retention); training runs on a single 8xB200 node for ~27 hours wall-clock, early-stopped at step 897 of a planned 2000-step budget.
evidence.value: 31,977 effective samples (47.7% retention); 27h on 8xB200; stop at step 897/2000
evidence.condition: LoRA + optimizer offload + vLLM-colocated rollout on ms-swift; CATM pipeline
evidence.source_locator: Section 3.6 PDF Page 5; Table 5 PDF Page 12

evaluation_context: Benchmark: SWE-Bench Verified (all 500 instances). Downstream agent: OpenHands with Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507, temperature 0, 100-round max; no-retrieval baseline 25.8% resolve / 23.0 rounds / 631K tokens per resolved issue (within one SD of publicly reported 25.2+-0.7%). Retriever: CodeGrep 14B built on Qwen3-14B-Instruct. Six configurations compared (baseline, BM25, Jina-1.5B, CodeGrep v1/v2/v3). Training hardware: single 8xB200 node, LoRA, ~27h. RL environment uses Git worktrees with up to 8 concurrent tool calls/turn, max 4 turns, tool-concurrency cap 64 (asyncio semaphore), max 32 tool execs per rollout. Efficiency accounting (Sec 5.3): headline Table 3 numbers are pooled per-config over its own resolved set (baseline 129, v3 135) and thus mix efficiency with a selection effect; a paired analysis on the 96 co-resolved instances preserves 60-80% of the pooled effect (-9% rounds, -15% tokens), confirming per-issue acceleration. A representative action-level trace (Sec 6, django-15278) shows injection converting a stalled 74-action/3.2M-token rollout with no patch into a 15-action/307K-token success (~10x fewer tokens).
limitations: Only one downstream agent stack is evaluated (OpenHands + Qwen3-30B-A3B), so generalization to Claude Code, Cursor, or Windsurf is untested. The benefit of dropping the line-range reward term is conjectured to be editor-interface dependent: agents whose editor consumes full files (OpenHands, Cursor) benefit, while agents whose editor consumes line ranges (plausibly Windsurf Cascade) may not. v1 matches v3's resolve rate (27.0%) but not its efficiency (-1.3% rounds, -0.6% tokens, essentially flat), showing resolve rate alone does not predict efficiency. The headline -15%/-19% efficiency figures are pooled and partly reflect a selection effect (v3 resolves 6 more instances than baseline); the paired -9%/-15% on co-resolved instances is the conservative estimate. Comparison to concurrent Cognition SWE-grep is necessarily partial because their reward formulation is not fully disclosed. Inference-time wall-clock latency is not reported; efficiency is measured only via rounds and tokens. CodeGrep's contribution is concentrated on rollout cost, not resolve rate (Sec 7).
project_relevance: Directly targets the agent-acceleration problem of repeated grep/glob/read exploration: it gives an open, trainable retriever that shortens the file-finding phase and reports the exact metrics the topic values (rounds, tokens, tool-call counts, resolve rate). The precision-threshold characterization (hurts/neutral/buys efficiency) is a portable design heuristic for deciding when retrieval injection into a coding agent will pay off. The advantage-layer (vs reward-layer) efficiency-scaling result is a transferable RL-training insight for any tool-policy reward mixing accuracy with efficiency. For a code-agent optimization path (search symbol -> read file -> locate call chain -> patch -> verify), this validates front-loading retrieval into a specialized submodule; the §5.3 paired accounting and §6 action trace show the savings come from compressing the exploratory prefix of repo-wide find/grep sweeps, not from supplying the fix.
source_notes: Primary source: arXiv 2608.05886v1 (fetched, FETCHED). Evidence Pack covers PDF Pages 1, 2, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12 (abstract, intro, related work, method 3.1-3.6, experiments 4.1-4.3, analysis 5.1-5.3, case study 6, limitations 7, appendix Table 5).
Resolve-rate and efficiency headline numbers in the abstract are corroborated by Table 3 / Section 4.3 with full baselines, so they are treated as verified experiment facts, not unverified claims.

Section 5.3 (PDF Page 8) qualifies the headline efficiency: pooled -15% rounds/-19% tokens mix a selection effect (baseline 129 vs v3 135 resolved); paired on 96 co-resolved instances the effect is -9% rounds/-15% tokens (60-80% of pooled).

Section 6 case study (django-15278, PDF Page 8): baseline 74 actions/3.2M tokens/no patch -> injection 15 actions/307K tokens/patch passes; CodeGrep compresses exploratory find/grep prefix, does not supply the fix itself.
Authors plan to release model, CATM pipeline, RL environment, and evaluation harnesses.
